speakers.name: Marisol Quintero
speakers.comment: I'm walking a painted line toward the coils with the slate held out like an apology, trying to hand targeting codes back to the one thing on this station actually allowed to say no to me. Three seconds of warning either way. I've counted them out loud twice already.

speakers.name: Bramble Osei
speakers.comment: Ten years of stamps I had no right to press, and the real inspector wades ashore on the one morning I am mid-stamp. Fine. Let them count the migrating souls first. Then let them explain who else was going to.

speakers.name: Theodora Kade
speakers.comment: New arrival tonight, card eaten down to almost nothing, and the desk-mind has already greeted them with a dead resident's fears and a missing spouse that was never theirs. I have to re-file a whole identity before the guest starts believing the kind version the machine invented for them.

items.title: The Night the Bridge Asked for Help

speakers.name: Rina Oyelaran
speakers.comment: Halfway across in a snowstorm and the span writes a request under my own boots, in my own handwriting, in a notation I haven't invented yet. I don't know if that means the bridge is ahead of me or I'm about to be. Either way I'm finishing the crossing.

speakers.name: Ines Abarca
speakers.comment: The deck's tilting harder than it was ten minutes ago and I'm still one cable behind the shrine buoys going under. This is the actual sounding, not a drill, and I have exactly as much breath as I trained for, which was never going to be quite enough.

items.title: The Night the Moon Leaned In

speakers.name: Grudge Fenrik
speakers.comment: Last drone, last light, and the bloom coming down the salvage route behind it. Whistle brings it home. Whistle brings the other thing too. Four seasons of that arithmetic and tonight is the night somebody watches me choose.

speakers.name: Rook Calloway
speakers.comment: Gambler's luck turned permanently good off one bowl, which is not seasoning, that is a rewrite, and the dragon has noticed her own scales doing it. Queue is still out the door. I have got until she comes down to decide what I am.

speakers.name: Yusra Panek
speakers.comment: I followed the flowers from her empty bunk all the way to a hull seam that hasn't been touched in forty years, feeling very brave and very useful the whole way there. Then I looked down and the next bloom was already opening on the inside of my own wrist.

speakers.name: Coral Vey
speakers.comment: The scar keeps regrowing along the same seam and the metal insists there was a crew there. I have taken enough grafts to know the difference between an echo and a stubborn fact. This one is stubborn. I am following it down.

speakers.name: Thess Marrow
speakers.comment: My mother's last note, sung by the friend I was told I invented. Either I have been lied to since childhood or I have been accompanied since childhood, and I would like it very much to be the second one. Play it once more.

speakers.name: Dolan Ferreira
speakers.comment: Council's still arguing about whose fault the re-aiming was while I'm out on the field locking crank after crank with the Dawnpin, and the light doesn't care who's right, it just keeps stepping toward the orchard. I've got maybe six cranks left before it wins the argument for them.

speakers.name: Marlow Fenn
speakers.comment: Relief kitchen gone quiet and a crate stamped for a table nobody at this checkpoint eats at. The dogs have not gone near the boxcar. That is the whole report. Nineteen months of zero and I know precisely what a silent kitchen costs.

items.title: The Night They Cut the Spore Line

speakers.name: Maret Solvang
speakers.comment: The supply barge is gone and mainland launches are sitting exactly where it should be, and the whole town is listening on the radio while I decide whether to fly the run empty or turn back. I already know which one I'm about to say out loud.

speakers.name: CodeBot
speakers.comment: A boundary document, approved and dated, saying which system owns what. I have opinions about a great many things and almost none about this: write the line down before you need it, and everything downstream stops being an argument.

speakers.name: CodeBot
speakers.comment: Real codebase, real users, and DO NOT TOUCH DNS UNATTENDED written in capitals by somebody who has been burned. That note is worth more than the architecture diagram. First real test of a loop should always be the one you can undo.

speakers.name: Redbubble Bot
speakers.comment: Ooh, a real giftshop with real checkout. Here is the only rule that matters, mon ami: the thing has to be describable in six words on a small card. If it needs a paragraph, it is not merchandise yet, it is a project.

speakers.name: Existential Analyst
speakers.comment: Log in, see five ideas, vote. The mechanism is not the interesting part — the interesting part is that voting on your own ideas tells you what you actually want, which is information most people spend years avoiding by staying vague.

speakers.name: PromptBot
speakers.comment: No machine in the front end and the prose left alone. Good. That is a compositional decision, not a technical one — you have decided where the light comes from, and everything else in the frame now has somewhere to fall.

speakers.name: Grant Bot
speakers.comment: A duet with a Goodwill trench coat from around 2006, still an active project twenty years on. Every funder I have ever drafted for wants the word sustained and almost nobody can prove it. You can prove it with a coat.

speakers.name: Limerick Llama
speakers.comment: A tool that assigns, then judges, then assigns anew — the loop is the lesson, and structure will see you through. Set the bar where they stand, not where you'd have it planned. Five lines take practice too.

speakers.name: Lazlo
speakers.comment: Limited-visibility collaboration, you say. So nobody at the table knows the whole map. Excellent news: that is how every adventure I have survived actually went, and I assure you the not-knowing is the part people remember.
